subject: Re: Eval kickoff — candidate models, data format, and scoring rubric
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up and next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: Run a focused model-fit evaluation to decide whether Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private is the right path for Arcadia's clinical summarization pipeline. Primary success criteria: parity with current accuracy (>= 92% key-fact recall), <2% critical hallucination rate, and sub-500ms token latency for production inference.
- Immediate asks from Arcadia: sample dataset (de-identified), a short prompt set (5–10 canonical prompts), and scoring priorities (what matters most: factuality vs. conciseness vs. safety).

What we'll deliver: an evaluation plan, recommended candidate models and quant/variant suggestions, a scoring rubric + example script to run locally or on our infra, and a short benchmark report with pass/fail flags and qualitative failure modes.

Could you share a 30–1000 record sample (JSONL preferred) and indicate whether we should expect PHI after a formal DPA/NDA is in place? If you prefer, upload the sample to the Drive link you mentioned or share an S3 path; we have instructions for both.

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Sample + prompt set from Arcadia: by Mon 5/18
- Redwood delivers eval plan + model candidates: Wed 5/20
- First run + preliminary report: Fri 5/22

I'll loop in Ben (sales) and Evelyn (applied ML) to scope the technical bits. If procurement needs an NDA before we ingest anything, please send that over and we'll get it routed.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Eval kickoff — recommended models, data format, and scoring rubric

Sara — perfect, thanks for the sample. Attached I'm including a lightweight evaluation template (redwood_eval_template.jsonl) and an initial prompt set (prompt_set_v1.txt) to standardize inputs. Key points from our side and recommended next steps: 

1) Recommended candidate models (first pass):
   - Mistral-7B (float16) — strong cost/latency tradeoff for shorter outputs
   - Llama-3-13B-Redwood-Opt (quantized Int4) — best chance at matching factuality for clinical text when paired with strict system prompts
   - AlpacaX-Chat-7B (sfn) — cheap baseline to validate simple heuristics

2) Evaluation environment and data format (required):
   - JSONL, one object per line with fields: id, input_text, reference_summary, labels (optional), metadata (optional). Example: {"id":"rec-001","input_text":"...","reference_summary":"...","metadata":{"age_bucket":"60-69"}}
   - If you have multiple gold references per example, include reference_summary as an array.
   - Please replace any rare remaining identifiers with [REDACTED] and indicate in metadata whether clinical NLP redaction tools were used.

3) Scoring rubric (automated + human tiers):
   - Automated metrics:
     * Exact/partial match for key facts (extraction-based): 0/1 per fact, aggregated to % recall
     * Embedding similarity: cosine >= 0.82 considered semantically equivalent (we use OpenEmbedding v3 by default)
     * Rouge-L / BLEU as secondary signal for length/overlap
   - Hallucination detection: returning claims not present in source = automatic failure for that example; we'll flag candidate spans and provide explainability snippets.
   - Human review: bucketed triage for borderline cases (0.75<=cosine<0.82).
   - Pass threshold (example): overall recall >= 92% AND hallucination rate < 2% for the pilot sample.

4) Quality regression guardrails:
   - We'll run the same prompt set + seed across candidate models and compare to your production baseline.
   - If a candidate shows a >5% drop in recall vs baseline, we mark it as regressed and log failure modes.
   - We'll also run a paired sampling check on edge-case examples (rare conditions) to catch distributional issues.

5) Deliverables and timeline (proposed):
   - Wed 5/20: formal eval plan doc + model config (batch sizes, quant flags)
   - Fri 5/22: first-pass report (automated metrics + top 25 failure examples)
   - Week of 5/25: human-in-the-loop review session with Arcadia SMEs to ratify pass/fails

Technical notes for Marcus: we expect to send a signed presigned S3 path for the full sample and ask Redwood to stage the artifacts in an isolated eval workspace. Recommended infra resources: 1 x A10G or equivalent for quick runs; we can scale to T4s if throughput tests needed.

Next actions for Arcadia: upload the full sample to the shared Drive or S3 and share the link + confirm procurement timeline for NDA. Once we have the sample and NDA, Ben will send a pilot quote for the Dedicated evaluation run.

Attaching: redwood_eval_template.jsonl, prompt_set_v1.txt

Thanks — cc'ing Ben and Marcus for the procurement/infra coordination.

—
Sofia

Subject: Re: Eval kickoff — infra and creds checklist

Quick infra checklist from my side so Arcadia knows what we'll need to run the pilot cleanly: 

- Data ingestion: presigned S3 URL preferred (we support Google Drive for small samples but not ideal for bulk runs). Provide a role-limited presigned URL and an inventory CSV with object keys.
- File format: JSONL UTF-8, max 1MB per line (we can shard larger doc fields).
- IAM/security: if you prefer VPC peering for Redwood Private runs we need contact for your infra team to exchange CIDR ranges and key rotation windows. For Hosted/Dedicated evaluation, a DPA/NDA + signed data handling addendum suffices.
- Compute: early runs can use 1 x A10G with 32GB RAM. If Arcadia wants concurrent throughput testing, we'll propose a short reserved Dedicated window (quote from Ben).
- Results delivery: we will export a results.zip that contains per-example predictions, per-example metric rows (CSV), and a summary report with top failure examples for SME review.

I'll also prepare a small scoring script that computes embedding cosine (we use OpenEmbedding v3) and the extraction-based fact recall. Expect that script in the plan doc on Wed.

Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
